title: Security vetting for critical information infrastructure personnel
asked: Whether the Ministry will introduce mandatory centralised government security vetting for personnel with access to Singapore's critical information infrastructure, and if not, how it ensures employer-led vetting, including of foreign nationals in sensitive technical roles, is robust against state-sponsored cyber threats.
response: Mrs Josephine Teo said insider threats are one of many threats to critical information infrastructure (CII). Under the Cybersecurity Act, CII owners must put in place access management controls, monitor for anomalies and suspicious activities, and investigate unauthorised activity. She said the Government will continue to review required standards and consider further enhancements. In supplementary replies, she said no profile should be assumed safer, vetting is not a silver bullet, and cybersecurity uses zero trust, least privileged access, monitoring of suspicious behaviour, and multiple layers of defence; where useful and relevant, measures are in place, but not all requirements are publicly revealed.

key_points.point: Under the Cybersecurity Act, CII owners must put in place access management controls and processes to monitor for anomalies and suspicious activities.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: owners of CIIs are required to put in place access management controls and processes to monitor for anomalies and suspicious activities in these systems

key_points.point: CII owners must investigate unauthorised activity once detected.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: Upon detection of any unauthorised activity, CII owners are required to investigate such anomalies.

key_points.point: The Government will continue to review the standards it requires and consider further enhancements.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: We will continue to review the standards we require and consider further enhancements that could be effective.

key_points.point: No particular profile of person with system access should be assumed more or less likely to commit nefarious activities.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: we should not assume that any particular profile of someone who is able to access the system is more or less likely to commit nefarious activities

key_points.point: Security vetting is not assumed to be a silver bullet.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: we also do not assume that security vetting is a silver bullet

key_points.point: Cybersecurity operates on the concept of zero trust.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: today we operate with the concept of zero trust

key_points.point: Where useful and relevant for certain cybersecurity accesses, measures are in place to ensure persons accessing them fit the right conditions.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: where it is useful and relevant to do so for certain types of cybersecurity accesses, yes, we do have measures in place to ensure that the persons accessing them fit the right conditions

key_points.point: The Government does not publicly reveal all the requirements it puts in place, for security reasons.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: we do not publicly reveal all the requirements that we put in place

key_points.point: Vetting exists but depends on the activity.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: It is not the case that there is no vetting. It depends on what the activity is.

left_open: Whether mandatory centralised government security vetting will be introduced for personnel with access to critical information infrastructure.
What specific assistance the Cyber Security Agency provides to private CII owners to verify the backgrounds of foreign nationals in sensitive technical roles.
Whether a tiered vetting system requiring Government-led G50 security clearance for personnel with super user or administrator access will be introduced.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on upstream personnel vetting, foreign nationals in sensitive roles, and aligning CII security clearance with public servants.
